record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can a cryptocurrency inflation-targeting regime define and track an adequate basket of goods and services when goods are usually denominated in national currencies, so measured purchasing-power fluctuations of a volatile cryptocurrency may mainly reflect exchange-rate variability?

evidence.quote:
Inﬂation targeting poses the obvious challenges of the
deﬁnition and tracking of an adequate basket of goods and
services. More importantly, goods usually are denominated
in some national currency. Purchasing power ﬂuctuations of
a volatile cryptocurrency measured by a basket of dollar
denominated goods should mainly be caused by exchange rate
variability. As a consequence inﬂation targeting and exchange
rate targeting would be close to equivalent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cryptocurrency C whose monetary authority (or protocol) wishes to implement an inflation-targeting regime. Inflation is to be measured by tracking the price, denominated in units of C, of a representative basket B = {(g_i, w_i)} of goods and services (with weights w_i ≥ 0 summing to 1). Assume that for each good g_i there is a price p_i^N(t) quoted in some national fiat currency N_i, and let e_{N_i,C}(t) denote the exchange rate from N_i to C at time t. Then the C-denominated price of the basket is

  P_B^C(t) = Σ_i w_i · p_i^N(t) · e_{N_i,C}(t),

and the measured inflation rate is π_C(t) = d/dt log P_B^C(t).

(a) Formulate a precise definition of an "adequate" basket B for the purpose of cryptocurrency inflation targeting, including criteria (e.g., representativeness of cryptocurrency-denominated economic activity, observability of prices, robustness to manipulation) under which π_C(t) measures intrinsic purchasing-power changes of C rather than mere exchange-rate variability against the fiat currencies N_i.

(b) Prove or disprove the following claim: if essentially all goods in B are quoted in a single fiat currency N, then inflation targeting (stabilizing π_C(t)) for C is functionally equivalent to exchange-rate targeting of e_{N,C}(t), in the sense that any monetary policy rule stabilizing one stabilizes the other up to bounded error.

(c) Propose and analyze a construction of a basket B (or a family of baskets) and an associated price index for which inflation targeting is provably distinct from exchange-rate targeting against any single fiat currency, and characterize the conditions on the joint dynamics of (p_i^N, e_{N_i,C}) under which this distinction is meaningful.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The question is posed as an open design challenge in the cryptocurrency monetary stabilization literature; subsequent work on stablecoins (e.g., Libra/Diem basket designs, algorithmic stablecoin proposals) discusses related issues but does not provide a definitive mathematical resolution of the basket-definition / inflation-vs-exchange-rate equivalence problem.

status_evidence.title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses inflation targeting challenges and the near-equivalence to exchange-rate targeting when goods are denominated in fiat.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as an open design question in cryptocurrency monetary policy.
